subject: HIPAA + SOC 2 discovery — BAA availability, PHI boundaries, hosting options
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Torres <lena.torres@cardiomed.org>, Tom Wilkes <tom.wilkes@carebridgehealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 25 Apr 2026 15:12:00 +0000
Subject: Call recap and next steps — BAA, PHI boundaries, hosting options

Hi Lena / Tom,

Thanks again for the time earlier — good discussion. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we all have alignment: 

Summary of what we heard from CardioMed:
- You expect to submit aggregated patient summaries from your routing layer, and a small subset of requests will include direct identifiers (name, MRN) tied to clinical notes.
- Retention policy: 30 days for cached inference state, longer-term data retention managed downstream; you need to confirm retention controls can be enforced.
- Required hosting posture: would prefer VPC/private hosting but asked whether Redwood Hosted API with a BAA could be acceptable for a scoped PHI workload.

What Redwood can offer (short):
- BAA availability: We do have a BAA we can sign with enterprise customers. See attached Redwood_BAA_Summary.pdf for scope and limitations.
- Deployment modes: Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) and Private (VPC / on-prem) are fully supported for PHI workloads. Hosted API with a signed BAA can be supported for limited PHI patterns, but depends on dataflow constraints and legal sign-off.
- SOC 2: Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II controls; I attached a short SOC2-Status-Summary.md with redacted scope items we commonly share.

Action items / asks for CardioMed before we can confirm a hosting recommendation:
1) Can you confirm the percentage of requests that include direct identifiers vs. de-identified text? A rough estimate is fine.
2) Please attach the vendor security questionnaire (we can start a redline).
3) Any hard constraints on data residency / region? You mentioned US only but wanted to confirm.

Next steps (proposed):
- Tom/Lena: send the vendor questionnaire and a sample request flow (anonymized).
- Redwood (me): I will route the questionnaire to Rishi (security) and Karthik (solutions) for answers and a short recommendation on deployment options.
- If needed, schedule a technical follow-up next week with your security team.

I've attached the vendor questionnaire stub we usually use + the BAA summary and SOC2 notes. Please let me know if a Tuesday or Wednesday call next week works for a 30-min technical sync.

Thanks,
Olga
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0192

Attachments: Redwood_BAA_Summary.pdf, Vendor_Security_Questionnaire.xlsx, SOC2-Status-Summary.md

From: Lena Torres <lena.torres@cardiomed.org>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 26 Apr 2026 09:34:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Call recap and next steps — BAA, PHI boundaries, hosting options

Thanks Olga — appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Identifier split: ~12% of requests will contain direct identifiers (name, MRN); the remainder is de-identified clinical text.
- Retention: We cannot accept any persistent storage of PHI beyond 90 days for audit logs; short-lived caches for inference (<=72 hours) are acceptable if encrypted at rest and access-controlled.
- Residency: US-only is required.

I attached CardioMed_Vendor_Q_Apr2026.xlsx — it's not exhaustive but covers our baseline questions (encryption, key management, access controls, notification SLA).

Regarding Hosted API + BAA: we are open to Hosted if you guarantee strict separation and can show controls around transient caching and key management.

Can Rishi or your security team confirm whether Hosted with BAA has been used for similar customers and what restrictions applied? Also please confirm SOC 2 scope items cover encryption-in-transit, encryption-at-rest, and change management.

Thanks — Lena
Director, Technical Operations | CardioMed Health
Lena.Torres@cardiomed.org

Attachment: CardioMed_Vendor_Q_Apr2026.xlsx

Attached: CardioMed_Vendor_Q_Apr2026.xlsx (from customer) + current Redwood_BAA_Summary.pdf

Olga

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 27 Apr 2026 08:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: FW: CardioMed vendor questionnaire — need deployment recommendation + SOC2 scope

Olga / Karthik — quick security response, happy to take the tech call if needed.

- SOC 2: Redwood currently maintains SOC 2 Type II (security & availability controls in-scope). The SOC2-Status-Summary.md covers the encryption-in-transit, encryption-at-rest, and our change management process that we share with prospects. We do not share the full report without an NDA, but the summary should satisfy CardioMed to proceed.

- Eligible deployment modes for PHI: Private (VPC) and Dedicated (customer-dedicated capacity) are fully supported for PHI workloads. Hosted API + BAA can be used in narrowly scoped situations but requires:
  * Approval from Legal (because of multi-tenant control plane elements),
  * Explicit contract language on caching TTLs (we can enforce short-term KV cache TTLs),
  * Proof of US-only region routing.

- Retention: We can enforce short-lived cache TTLs (configurable) and provide audit logging; long-term retention policies (e.g., 90 days for logs) are possible but require confirmation on log aggregation pipelines and who manages keys.

Next steps from security:
1) I'll review CardioMed's questionnaire and fill items related to encryption, key mgmt (we use KMS + customer-managed keys for Private), access control, and incident SLA.
2) Recommend a technical sync with CardioMed's security team — propose Tue 2026-04-28 16:00 UTC (please confirm).

Short answer to Lena: Hosted + BAA is not a blanket yes for all PHI; Dedicated or Private are the safer, faster path to go-live. If CardioMed is willing to accept a scoped Hosted approach we can map required contractual and technical guardrails.

Rishi
Director, Security Engineering | Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai

- Rishi confirms: SOC 2 Type II in place (summary attached). Private (VPC) and Dedicated are fully cleared for PHI. Hosted + BAA is possible only under a scoped agreement with legal and short TTLs on caches — not recommended if you need rapid go-live.
- We can enforce US-only routing and configurable cache TTLs (we typically set 24–72 hours by workload).

Proposed next steps:
1) We will complete CardioMed's questionnaire (attached filled version will follow).
2) Schedule a 30-min technical sync — Rishi proposed Tue 28 Apr 2026 16:00 UTC. Does that time work for your security team?
3) If CardioMed wants the fastest path to production, we recommend Dedicated (reserved capacity) while legal finalizes the BAA for longer-term Private deployment.

I'll upload the filled questionnaire and a redline of the BAA summary by EOD today. If the Tue slot doesn't work, propose alternatives.

Thanks,
Olga
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
